findings.reason: the author must either exclude tight-cropped files' exported ratio from the invariant and state what the record shows for them, or anchor the invariant on the drawn canvas ratio, because as written no landed export of those four scripts can pass the measure.
findings.text: "each figure file's exported width-to-height ratio is unchanged within one part in a thousand" is unachievable for the figures §2 requires to move, and contradicts the same section's Delivers sentence: scripts/plot_jet_epoch_evolution.py and scripts/plot_jet_poloidal.py export with `bbox_inches="tight"` (e.g. lines 289, 514, 1026; 380, 457), so today's exported ratio is the content crop, not the drawn canvas ratio — tracked files show the gap: docs/images/jet_wall_limiter_evolution.png is 3110x1223 (ratio 2.54) against an 18x6 in canvas (3.00), and docs/images/jet_limiter_contours.png is 3803x2029 (1.87) against 20x10 in (2.00), i.e. 2%-15% away from the canvas ratio. Routing those exports through a shared function that writes the canvas changes the exported ratio by far more than one part in a thousand, while reproducing the crop instead makes the measured ratio depend on live graph content (the scripts fetch epochs from the knowledge graph), so the tracked "before" image cannot be matched to one part in a thousand even with unchanged code. The Delivers sentence's "same drawn aspect ratio" and the done-when's "exported ratio unchanged" therefore cannot both hold for those four scripts' files, and a worker is left without a satisfiable measure
